questions.question: What does MySQL store when you create a view?
options: Only the view's SELECT definition; results are merged or materialized at query time
A materialized copy of the rows, refreshed automatically on every write
A materialized copy refreshed nightly by the Event Scheduler
An index over the base tables' columns
questions.explanation: MySQL has no materialized views. A view is a stored query that is either merged into the outer query or materialized into a temporary table per statement.

questions.question: A view is defined with `WHERE city = 'Mumbai' WITH CHECK OPTION`. What happens on `INSERT INTO the_view (name, city) VALUES ('Ravi', 'Pune')`?
options: The row is inserted but is not visible through the view
The insert fails because the new row would not satisfy the view's WHERE clause
The city is silently changed to 'Mumbai'
Views can never accept INSERT statements
questions.explanation: WITH CHECK OPTION rejects inserts and updates that would produce rows the view cannot see (error 1369).

questions.question: What is `DELIMITER //` in a stored procedure script?
options: A server-side setting stored with the procedure
Part of the CREATE PROCEDURE syntax required by every driver
A command for the mysql client so the semicolons inside the routine body do not end the statement early
A way to declare a comment block
questions.explanation: DELIMITER is interpreted by the mysql command-line client and is never sent to the server; drivers and GUI tools do not need it.

questions.question: With binary logging on and log_bin_trust_function_creators off, why might CREATE FUNCTION fail with error 1418?
options: Functions cannot use DECIMAL return types
Functions must always declare OUT parameters
Functions are disabled when binary logging is enabled
The function was not declared DETERMINISTIC, NO SQL or READS SQL DATA
questions.explanation: MySQL requires one of these characteristics for safe replication. DETERMINISTIC is an unchecked promise, so declaring it falsely can cause wrong results.
